reason: E1 shows Hf improves room-temperature properties in single-phase FCC HEAs via precipitation, but explicitly notes these studies use >1 at.% Hf and focus on room temperature, not high-temperature refractory alloys. E2 only provides general background on HEAs without mentioning Hf. The key premises about high-temperature behaviour, the specific <1 at.% addition, and applicability to refractory alloys are unsupported by the cited evidence.
premises: Hf addition to single-phase FCC HEAs improves room-temperature properties via precipitation of Ni7Hf2 and Laves phases
Hf is an essential element for interface strengthening in superalloys and strengthening of Ni-Al B2 phase
The proposed mechanism (precipitation and interface strengthening) will operate in refractory HEAs at high temperature
Small Hf addition (<1 at.%) will not significantly reduce ductility
The benefits observed in FCC HEAs and superalloys will translate to refractory HEAs for jet-turbine applications
